memory_candidates.content: BracketFormula negation via prepend at first alpha_0 occurrence r_0 is UNSOUND for x_0 > r_0: rightPart.holds(x_0, z_1) does not imply rightPart.holds(r_0, z_1) because the first segment widens from (x_0, w_1) to (r_0, w_1) without beta_1 info on the extra piece. Five approaches were tried and all fail: (1) prepend with alpha_0.neg, (2) prepend with alpha_0.neg.conj beta_0, (3) segment-failure decomposition, (4) F-chain approach, (5) split-at-every-position. The correct approach uses VecEA2 endpoint convention where alpha_0 is at the FIXED endpoint z_0, eliminating x_0 > r_0.

The F-chain characterization (bracket_implies_fChainPred) is genuinely one-directional for the full bracket biconditional. Forward: bf.holds → orderedPointsExist 1 fChainPred (proved). Backward: orderedPointsExist → bf.holds is FALSE because (1) fChainPred omits beta_0, (2) Until witnesses may exceed z1. Counter-example: bf with beta_0=False, alpha_0=True has bf.holds=False but orderedPointsExist 1 fChainPred=True. The V constructed from Lemma 5.3 applied to fChainPred gives V.holds → ¬bf.holds (correct) but ¬bf.holds does NOT imply V.holds. For the backward direction of neg_partialBracketExist_is_vbracket, the same issue arises.
